As a maintenance mechanic, you will work in a large, fully automated distribution centre where technology is constantly in motion. Conveyor systems, roller conveyors, lifts and other automated installations ensure that enormous volumes of goods are moved throughout the warehouse. If a system comes to a standstill, that is where your work becomes interesting: identifying the cause of the problem and getting the system back up and running as quickly as possible.You will work with a broad combination of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and control technology. One fault may be caused by a mechanical component, while the next may require electrical troubleshooting or analysing the control system. You will look beyond simply replacing a faulty component: you will determine the root cause and identify what is needed to resolve the issue properly.Using advanced monitoring applications, you can see what is happening within the system and systematically identify technical and system-related faults. You will carry out repairs and maintenance and accurately document significant breakdowns and maintenance activities.It is precisely this combination that makes the role so interesting: rather than working on a single machine, you will work with an entire automated system in which different technologies come together. Do you have experience as a process operator in the food industry, technical insight, and are you ready to take the next step in your career?Hoe ziet jouw werkdag eruit?You start your day by going through the production schedule and then flush the machines with water before starting production. Together with your colleagues, you ensure that the correct materials are ready and that the production lines are operational. Using the forklift, you ensure that all products are in the right place.  You set up machines, monitor the parameters and carry out quality tests. You record and document all your findings. If you notice a deviation or a fault, you look for a solution and make adjustments where necessary. You also carry out minor technical maintenance and contribute ideas for improvements. At the end of the day, you get to work cleaning the machine so that production can start again the following day.  You'll work with various machines and production lines, which keeps your work nicely varied. Step by step, as a trainee all-round process operator, you'll get to know all the processes and, within 6 to 12 months, you'll progress to become a fully-fledged All-round Process Operator.  Specifically, you'll spend 25 % of your time on cleaning, 25 % on quality and parameter checks and 50 % operating the machines. Wat breng je mee?     - A completed MBO 4 qualification, preferably in a technical field (Process Operator, VAPRO, MAS or MTS) or demonstrable experience in the field;     - Experience as an operator in the food industry;     - Technical understanding and an interest in improving production processes;     - An independent, meticulous and eager-to-learn approach to work;     - A good command of Dutch and/or English;     - A forklift licence or a willingness to obtain one;     - Willingness to work shifts, excluding night shifts.
